title: Crispy Rice Salad with Gochujang Mushrooms
style: Bold, umami-rich salad with crispy rice, spicy mushrooms, and creamy peanut sauce
description: Crispy baked rice paired with savory gochujang mushrooms, fresh vegetables, and a creamy, zesty peanut sauce for a satisfying plant-based meal.
steps: Prepare the Crispy Rice: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F (fan). Toss cooked rice with chili oil and spread in a thin layer on a lined baking tray.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crisp. Let cool slightly, then lightly crush to break up large clumps.
Prepare the Mushrooms: Slice king oyster mushroom caps and shred the stems with a fork. Trim and separate the shimeji mushrooms.
Marinate: Mix gochujang, tamari, maple syrup, and rice vinegar into a paste. Add mushrooms and toss well to coat.
Cook the Mushrooms: Heat a large pan over medium heat. Cook mushrooms for about 10 minutes until they release moisture.
Once mostly dry, add sesame oil and cook undisturbed for 2 minutes to brown. Stir, then repeat to develop deeper colour and flavour.
Make the Peanut Sauce: Blend peanut butter, ginger, garlic, lime juice, tamari, maple syrup, dairy-free milk, and gochujang until smooth.
Assemble: Divide edamame, cucumber, spring onions, avocado, mint, mushrooms, and crispy rice between bowls.
Drizzle generously with peanut sauce and serve.
tips: Use day-old rice for the best crispy texture.
Don’t overcrowd the tray when baking rice — it needs space to crisp.
Let mushrooms sit undisturbed in the pan to develop deep browning.
Keep the sauce separate if storing leftovers to maintain texture.
Swap peanut butter for tahini to make the dish nut-free.
Brown rice works well if you prefer a chewier texture.
